title: Winter Mountain Leader (I) (Col to Capt) FMOS, CG TECOM
raw_text:
3.     MOS 0942, Winter Mountain Leader (I) (Col to Capt) FMOS, CG TECOM

    a. Summary. The WML performs duties of the unit mountain leader who is
the subject matter expert in mountain warfare tactics, techniques, and
procedures (such as over-the-snow mobility and avalanche hazard assessment),
acts as an advisor to the commander, and is capable of conducting pre-
environment training for their units.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Students must be fit for full duty.

            (2) Open to operating force MOSs Col through Capt.

            (3) Students must complete a first class PFT adjusted for altitude on
T-1.

        (4) Volunteers are recommended due to the intensity level and
demanding nature of this training.

        (5) Students must have no personal issues (legal, financial, etc.) as
this training center is remote and no time will be provided in the course for
such issues.

        (6) Students must be medically qualified to participate in a
demanding physical training program at high altitude (G6PD and sickle cell
screened) and be free of chronic or acute orthopedic injuries.

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the Winter Mountain Leaders
Course (M24M7B1) at the Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center,
Bridgeport, CA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (dj), Mountain Warfare Operations Training and Readiness Manual.




                                          1-56                       Enclosure (1)
 1111                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators.
